validity.summary: Existence, classification, and singleton status all confirmed -- no duplicate/relabel risk found.
validity.details: P6690 is confirmed as a real, existing, operating trunk gas transmission pipeline (105 km, 219 mm) from the Zapadno-Ozernoye gas field to Anadyr, Chukotka, operated by Sibneft-Chukotka LLC (100% subsidiary structure per Owner fill), corroborated by the operator's own site, an independent 2024 trade-journal article, contemporaneous 2003 construction-era news coverage, and an independent 2020 academic thesis -- four source lineages in total, all describing the same single pipeline. Checked against the batch's other-pipeline roster: no other Kamchatka/Chukotka-region row describes this same field-to-city route, confirming the pre-classification as a singleton (not a duplicate/relabel of another roster row). Location field values carried a typo ('Chukotka Autonomus District') corrected in the Location fill to 'Chukotka Autonomous Okrug', sourced 3 ways.
validity.recommended_action: No action needed beyond the fills already staged.

validity.summary: Length recorded as 105 km (sheet value, matched by 2 independent as-built-quality sources) conflicts with 115 km stated twice, consistently, in an independent 2020 academic (TPU) thesis.
validity.details: sibneft.org (the pipeline operator's own infrastructure page) states the line is 'протяженностью 105000 метров' (105,000 m = 105 km), and energypolicy.ru (2024, independent trade/academic journal, verified via Wayback) independently corroborates 'протяженностью 105 км' with the same 219 mm diameter -- two independent, current, as-built-quality sources agreeing exactly. However, a 2020 Tomsk Polytechnic University engineering thesis on the Zapadno-Ozernoye field (an independent academic source, verified via Wayback) states the pipeline route length as 115 km in two separate passages ('Длина трассы составляет 115 км' and 'по газопроводу длиной 115 км'), internally consistent with itself but not with the other two sources. Possible explanations not resolved by available evidence: the TPU figure may measure a slightly different route/endpoint definition (e.g. including the field gathering/UKPG internal piping, or a different as-designed vs as-built length), or one of the figures may simply be an error/rounding in one source lineage. Recommendation: keep 105 km as the recorded value (backed 2:1 by the more current, more directly operator-sourced figures) but do not treat the conflict as resolved -- a future pass with access to as-built engineering drawings or a Rosreestr pipeline registry entry could adjudicate it definitively.
validity.recommended_action: Keep LengthKnown=105.00 km as recorded (2 independent current sources agree); note the unresolved 115 km figure from the TPU thesis for a future pass.

validity.summary: Task brief's lead 'the line feeds the Anadyr CHP since ~2008' is very likely a conflation and should NOT be entered anywhere as a sourced fact about this pipeline (P6690).
validity.details: Investigated this lead specifically and found it does not hold up. energypolicy.ru (2024) states explicitly that gas from the Zapadno-Ozernoye field reaches Anadyr via THIS pipeline ('МГ «Западно-Озерное ГМ – г. Анадырь»', operated by Sibneft-Chukotka), but that partial conversion of the ANADYR CHP (Анадырская ТЭЦ) to this gas only began in 2018, under a 2016-2020 regional energy-efficiency program, and required building a SEPARATE, additional 7-km spur pipeline plus a new gas-distribution point specifically to reach the CHP plant site ('Для этого был проложен 7-километровый газопровод к территории ТЭЦ, построен газораспределительный пункт'). Separately, the 2020 TPU thesis describes gas from the wells reaching an 'Анадырская газомоторная станция' (Anadyr gas-motor/power station, 30 MW) via the 115 km line, noting this station 'при необходимости может обеспечить замещение Анадырской ТЭЦ' (can, if needed, substitute for/back up the Anadyr CHP) -- i.e. capability to substitute, not a statement that the CHP itself is fed by this line. No source supports a ~2008 CHP-feed date for P6690 itself. The true CHP connection is (a) a different, later (2018) project and (b) most plausibly a different, short spur pipeline not currently identified as any existing GEM row -- worth flagging to the orchestrator as a possible Discovery lead (see summary), though it is not tied to any pipeline PID on this batch's roster and so is not filed as a cross_row_leads entry.
validity.recommended_action: Do not record 'feeds Anadyr CHP since ~2008' anywhere for P6690. If GEM's existing wiki/infobox narrative implies this, it should be corrected to: the pipeline supplies Anadyr's gas-distribution/gas-motor station; the CHP itself was connected separately via a 2018-built 7 km spur, not part of this row.

Searched for a distinct pipeline PROPOSAL/announcement date (as opposed to construction or startup). Checked: sibneft.org's own company-history page (about/nasha_istoriya/) -- describes Sibneft-Chukotka LLC's 2001 founding as a JV between Sibneft and Chukotskaya Trading Company, with the latter contributing the Zapadno-Ozernoye field license to charter capital, and first OIL production in April 2004 at a DIFFERENT field (Verkhne-Telekaiskoye) -- no explicit pipeline proposal statement. The 2003-07-29 vsluh.ru/regnum.ru news item (earliest dated primary source found) already describes active construction underway (UKPG since January 2003) with no retrospective proposal/announcement date given. The 2020 TPU thesis discusses the field's design-document history (earliest reserve-approval reference: протокол ЦКЗ МПР РФ №157, undated year visible in the extract) but does not separately date a pipeline PROPOSAL as distinct from its eventual construction/technical-scheme approval (25.12.2007, itself a field-development-scheme approval, not a pipeline-specific proposal). No source gives a standalone proposal/announcement date for the pipeline itself. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than inferring one from the adjacent 2001 JV-formation or 2003 construction-start dates.

Genuinely conflicting/ambiguous evidence, not a search failure -- documenting the full timeline rather than guessing a single year. (1) A contemporaneous 2003-07-29 news item (vsluh.ru, syndicating a Stroytransgaz/ОАО «Сибнефть» press item, live-verified) reports UKPG (gas treatment unit) construction underway since January 2003, with the connecting pipeline to Anadyr ('низконапорный газопровод, который соединит комплекс газовых объектов Западно-Озерного ГНКМ и г. Анадырь') still to be LAID, expected to enable gas production 'in the coming year' [2004] -- i.e. as of mid-2003 the export pipeline itself had NOT yet been built, only planned/about to start. (2) The 2020 TPU thesis states the field's design-basis document ('Технологическая схема разработки') was approved by протокол ЦКР Роснедра по ЯНАО №60-07 от 25.12.2007, and separately states that by the date of analysis 'построен трубопровод внешнего транспорта газа «Западно-Озерное месторождение – г.Анадырь»' (the export pipeline HAS been built) as part of realizing that scheme's provisions -- implying the pipeline's actual construction/completion came substantially later than the 2003-2004 target, plausibly clustered around 2007-2008 (see Start [ref] notes on well trial-production dates). I could not pin down a single confirmed construction START or COMPLETION year bridging this gap (the project appears to have been significantly delayed from its original ~2003-2004 schedule to something closer to 2007-2008) and am not willing to guess a specific year/month from these two bracketing data points. Leaving UNRESOLVED; a future pass with access to Rosreestr/Glavgosexpertiza construction-permit records, or a corporate history document from Sibneft-Chukotka itself, could likely resolve this precisely.

IMPORTANT: this fill also corrects the task brief's lead ('the line feeds the Anadyr CHP since ~2008'), which I found to be a conflation -- see the dedicated validity[] concern and the status_reviews[] entry for the full correction. On the startup-date question itself: evidence spans a genuine multi-year range with no single clean answer. (1) The 2003-07-29 vsluh.ru news item projects gas PRODUCTION beginning 'in the coming year' (i.e. 2004) once the low-pressure connecting line to Anadyr was laid -- this was a projection, not a confirmed start. (2) The 2020 TPU thesis gives concrete WELL trial-production dates that are later and staggered: well No.103 trial production 2007, well No.101 2008, wells No.102/No.104 2008-2009 (extracted from two separate passages in the thesis that agree with each other). (3) The same thesis notes the field's official development-scheme approval (протокол ЦКР Роснедра по ЯНАО №60-07) is dated 25.12.2007, and separately states the field 'не вышло на технологические показатели в 2010 году проекта ОПЭ' (did not reach its 2010 pilot-development design targets) due to offtake limits imposed by Chukotenergo (the receiving utility) -- confirming the ramp-up was slow and non-linear, not a single clean start date. No source states an explicit pipeline (as opposed to well) in-service/start-flowing date. Given (a) the 2003-2004 projection was evidently not met on schedule, (b) actual well trial production is documented 2007-2009, and (c) I have no source pinning the PIPELINE's own first-gas date distinctly from the wells', I am not willing to select a single StartYear1 from this range. Leaving UNRESOLVED. If forced to estimate for internal purposes only (NOT entered as a value here), 2007-2008 is the best-supported window, consistent with -- but NOT the same claim as -- the debunked 'feeds Anadyr CHP since ~2008' lead: the well/pipeline startup and the (separate, later, 2018) Anadyr CHP connection are two different facts that appear to have been conflated in the original brief.

No pipeline THROUGHPUT/design-capacity figure was found in any source. The only quantitative production figure found is a 2003 vsluh.ru news projection of FIELD output ('Объем промышленной добычи на месторождении составит около 120 миллионов кубометров газа в год' -- approx. 120 million m3/year of field gas production), which is (a) a field-level production TARGET, not a pipeline capacity/design-throughput spec, (b) a 2003 forward-looking projection that the TPU thesis's own account of the field failing to reach its 2010 ОПЭ design targets (due to Chukotenergo offtake limits) suggests was not realized as planned, and (c) not attributable to the pipeline's engineered capacity even if realized -- field production and pipeline capacity are not interchangeable quantities without an explicit statement equating them, which no source provides. sibneft.org's own transport-infrastructure page (the row's best/most current source) gives no capacity figure at all, only physical specs (length, diameter, pressure, temperature). energypolicy.ru (2024) likewise gives no capacity/throughput number. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than substituting the stale, mismatched field-production figure as a pipeline Capacity value.

No segment-specific construction cost figure was found for this pipeline in any source checked (sibneft.org, energypolicy.ru, the 2003 vsluh.ru/regnum.ru news item, or the 2020 TPU thesis). The TPU thesis contains only a generic PER-WELL economic-model line item ('Сбор и транспорт газа, млн. руб./скв' -- gas gathering-and-transport cost per well, an aggregated per-well planning assumption used in its own investment-appraisal model), which is not a stated total or per-km construction cost for the pipeline itself and is not usable as a SegmentCost value without fabricating an attribution the source does not make. Leaving UNRESOLVED.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=operating is confirmed current as of the most recent evidence found: energypolicy.ru (2024 trade/academic journal article, verified live and via a 2025-07-08 Wayback capture) describes the pipeline in the present tense as actively transporting gas from Zapadno-Ozernoye to Anadyr, operated by Sibneft-Chukotka LLC, and describes an ADDITIONAL 2018-built spur (separate from this line) that further extended gas use to partially convert the Anadyr CHP -- i.e. the broader gas-supply system this pipeline anchors was still being actively expanded and used as recently as 2018-2024, strong evidence of continued/growing operation, not decline or retirement. sibneft.org's own current operations page (accessed live this session) likewise describes the pipeline in the present tense with full current specs. No indication of any outage, decommissioning, or status change found in any source. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the task brief's lead ('the line feeds the Anadyr CHP since ~2008'): this is very likely a conflation. The actual CHP connection is a separate, later (2018) 7 km spur pipeline built under a 2016-2020 regional energy-efficiency program -- not this pipeline, and not ~2008. What IS true is that gas from the wells (trial production 2007-2009 per an independent 2020 academic thesis) has long reached an Anadyr gas-motor/power station via this 105/115 km trunk line, and that station is described as CAPABLE of substituting for the CHP if needed -- a capability statement, not a feed-since-2008 fact. See the dedicated 'attribution' validity[] concern for full detail and sourcing. No proposed_changes -- verdict is a straight confirm of the current Status value.
